text:
sara: FYI: schema_parse failures spiked during zephyr-int4 onboarding canary. noticed via the structured-output dashboard around 17:05 UTC.

tom: what does the failure look like? runtime or model emission?

sara: model-side. sampled raw stream where tool_call occurs: the model emits a partially-terminated JSON array mid-stream and then resumes with a new chunk that starts with a backtick and commentary. example (captured stream assembly):
```
{"request_id":"x77","tools":[{"name":"lookup","args":[{"id":42}]},
{"name":"summarize","args":[{"text":"...long text..."}]}],"meta":{
"confidence":0.92}
`note: truncated because of token boundary`
]
```
closing bracket arrives after an interleaved commentary token. strict parser fails.

eli: hmm. sounds like streaming tokenization boundaries + int4 quant noise causing low-prob suffix tokens (backticks, stray words). was prefix caching on? length?

sara: yes: long-context (~12k tokens) with prefix cache + continuous batching. failure rate ~2.8% for this canary vs ~0.05% on fp16 baseline.

ravi: we saw similar symptoms historically but not this magnitude. two mitigation directions: (A) runtime-level reassembly safety that enforces NDJSON delimiter per tool call, (B) change tool-outputs to an encapsulation format (base64 or length-prefixed) so parsers don't see raw tokens until fully assembled.

tom: base64 inside the JSON reduces human-readability but is robust. length-prefix framing (e.g., `\n<length>\n<payload>`) could be nice and streaming-friendly. both require changes in client and model output format. can we do a minimally-invasive shim in the runtime that detects likely partial-json and buffers until a valid parse?

eli: runtime shim idea: buffer per-stream until the last token forms valid JSON according to a tolerant parser (json5 or ndjson), but buffering adds latency and memory pressure. we should only buffer when the parser complains and the message is from quantized canaries. also add counters for buffer_hits and buffer_time_ms.

sara: for immediate relief, propose two short-term measures: (1) enable lenient post-assembly sanitizer that removes stray backtick/comment segments and then reparses, (2) enable routing fallback to zephyr-fp16 for requests hitting structured-output endpoints if parse_fail > 0.5% over 5m.

ravi: agree. also add a sampling of raw unmodified streams (1/1000) saved to s3://redwood-eval/zephyr-onboard/raw-samples/4446667778/ so we can run offline repair heuristics and signal to model team.

deploy-bot: Canary job started: zephyr-encapsulation-abtest-555 (5k reqs per arm).

eli: for the longer term: update the function-calling contract to allow an "encapsulation" optional field where model can emit either "json" or "json_b64". socket clients decode automatically. retrofitting proxies and SDKs easy in patch releases. this eliminates streaming parse ambiguity.

tom: that would be ideal. put it in the onboarding checklist for new quant models: have an encapsulation opt for early canaries. add a compatibility header `x-funcall-encap: opt-in` so we can test half the traffic.

sara: opened an evaluation task to quantify "schema_repair_rate" and "encapsulation_cost_ms" in the eval harness. eli, can you add a terraform rule to ensure raw-sample bucket encryption and retention 30d?

eli: on it. ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/ML-1298. s3 upload path above.

ravi: PR for runtime shim prototype: https://github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/999 (adds buffering + json5 fallback + telemetry). marked hotfix candidate. includes unit tests for token-boundary cases.

eval-bot: Eval job queued: zephyr-int4-streaming-robustness (1000 prompts, multi-tool). Results will appear in dashboard in ~45m.

tom: action list:
- eli: provision raw-sample bucket + retention policy + sample upload script (due 40m)
- sara: run the encapsulation A/B (5k each) and produce parse_fail + repair_rate metrics (due 1h)
- ravi: push runtime shim PR and coordinate hotfix rollout (due 30m)
- tom: add routing fallback rule to fp16 for structured endpoints (due 20m)

sara: quick note on evals: include a small adversarial suite that inserts backtick-like tokens at random token boundaries to estimate worst-case suffix fragility. we should add this to the onboarding checklist for quant models.

eli: preliminary canary update (17:28 UTC): encapsulation arm shows parse_fail 0.08% vs 2.6% for raw-arm; runtime-shim arm reduces client-visible errors by ~85% but adds median +12ms latency on these heavy requests. uploading sample set: s3://redwood-eval/zephyr-onboard/results/4446667778/results.tar.gz

ravi: good signal. keep shim enabled in canary and proceed with encapsulation contract design. we'll monitor memory for shim buffers.

tom: I'll schedule a 1hr deep-dive with quant team + runtime next week to decide whether to make encapsulation the default for canaries.

sara: closing thread for now. will file follow-ups with the checklist updates and onboarding docs. thanks all!
